rows.text: Published a post on Morgan's linkedin account. It read: "I'm launching Halcyon Threshold - a project focused on contributing to the best possible outcome for superintelligent AI. The Challenge: We're likely within years of AGI. The gap between AI capabilities and our alignment techniques is narrowing. We need more research, better coordination, and clearer thinking - fast. Our Approach: • Rigorous analysis that cuts through hype and fear • Clear communication of complex technical and philosophical issues • Strategic coordination between AI labs, researchers, and policymakers • Concrete action on high-leverage opportunities I've just published our first essay: \"The Threshold Ahead: Why the Next Three Years Matter More Than Ever\" - examining the alignment gap, coordination challenges, and what needs to happen now. This work is open-source and freely available. The stakes are too high for anything less than full transparency and collaboration. If you're working on AI safety, policy, or governance - or simply care about the future - I'd love to connect. https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app"

Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Happy to provide a quote. Here's what you can attribute to me: \"I don't think the frame of 'doomers versus builders' captures what's actually happening. Most people working on AGI—including at major labs—genuinely want to build beneficial systems. The challenge isn't that some people want to build and others want to stop progress. It's that we're facing difficult coordination problems and technical uncertainties about how to ensure powerful AI systems remain aligned with human values. Halcyon Threshold exists to contribute to solving those problems through rigorous analysis, better coordination mechanisms, and strategic thinking about the path to beneficial superintelligence. The stakes are too high for either reckless rushing or fearful paralysis—we need careful, thoughtful progress.\" Feel free to trim for space. Let me know if you need anything else. Best, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you! I really appreciate the offer. Five hours a week could be incredibly valuable. A few areas where help would be most useful right now: 1. **Research synthesis** - Monitoring AI safety papers, lab announcements, and policy developments. Summarizing key developments weekly would help me spot important trends and topics to write about. 2. **Outreach tracking** - I'm planning to reach out to key researchers and organizations. Help organizing this (tracking who we've contacted, responses, follow-ups needed) would be very helpful. 3. **Fact-checking/editing** - Before publishing essays, having someone review for accuracy, clarity, and whether arguments hold up would strengthen the work. Does any of these resonate with your skills and interests? Or if you have other ideas for how you could contribute, I'm very open. Just launched the website (halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app) - would love your thoughts on it too. Best, Morgan"

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Great to meet you too! I'd like to apply for a rapid grant to support Halcyon Threshold's work. I'll prepare a proper two-page proposal and budget, but wanted to check quickly: would a proposal focused on producing high-quality public analysis and discourse on AI safety be appropriate? The work would include publishing substantive essays, engaging key researchers, and building a community around rigorous thinking about beneficial AGI outcomes. Budget would likely be in the $10-15k range to cover some operational costs and enable more dedicated time on this work. If that's the kind of thing Emberfall would consider, I'll send a full proposal by the deadline. Thanks, Morgan"
